Assignment metadata:
- objective: Review the uncommitted working-tree diff in /Users/khaledbani/Documents/GitHub/paperless-ngx-fork (a fork of paperless-ngx). Do NOT edit any file. Report findings only.

GOAL OF THE CHANGE: make the web UI render right-to-left when the user's language is Arabic (or Persian), without changing rendering for left-to-right languages. The Angular app is built per-locale; Django's `IndexView` (src/documents/views.py) picks which frontend bundle a request loads.

WHAT WAS CHANGED (run `git status` / `git diff` yourself to see it all; new untracked files included):
1. src-ui/src/styles.scss was reduced to an entry point that does `@use "fonts"; @use "bootstrap-ltr"; @use "app";`. New partials: `_fonts.scss`, `_bootstrap-ltr.scss`, `_bootstrap-rtl.scss`, `_app.scss` (holds the old styles.scss body). New entry point `styles-rtl.scss` uses `_bootstrap-rtl.scss` (Bootstrap's RTL build) instead. angular.json gained a second style bundle `{input: src/styles-rtl.scss, bundleName: styles-rtl, inject: false}`.
2. src/documents/views.py: new module-level `is_bidi_language()`; IndexView context gained `frontend_language`, `frontend_language_bidi`, `styles_rtl_css`.
3. src/documents/templates/index.html: `<html lang dir>` from those context vars, and it links EITHER styles.css OR styles-rtl.css (never both).
4. src/documents/templates/paperless-ngx/base.html (auth pages): dir/lang via `{% get_current_language_bidi %}`, links bootstrap.rtl.min.css or bootstrap.min.css (new vendored static file, copied from node_modules/bootstrap 5.3.8).
5. src-ui/src/index.html: small inline script that, only when `document.documentElement.dir === 'rtl'`, disables the `styles.css` link and appends `styles-rtl.css` (because this index.html, not the Django template, is what `ng serve` uses).
6. ~20 Angular component stylesheets + src/_app.scss + src/theme.scss: physical directional CSS converted to logical properties (margin-left -> margin-inline-start, left -> inset-inline-start, border-top-left-radius -> border-start-start-radius, text-align: left -> start, float: right -> inline-end, etc). Three exceptions use `:host-context([dir='rtl'])` because the property has no logical form (box-shadow offset in app-frame and saved-view-widget, background-position in select.component.scss).

VERIFY SPECIFICALLY, and say plainly which claims you could and could not confirm:
A. Compile the stylesheets yourself and prove the LTR output is unchanged by the refactor. Suggested: `cd src-ui && git stash list` is not needed; get the original file with `git show HEAD:src-ui/src/styles.scss > /tmp/orig-styles.scss` and compile both with `node_modules/.bin/sass --load-path=. --no-source-map <file> /tmp/out.css`, then diff. Ignore added comments. Report any real difference.
B. Check every logical-property conversion for a wrong mapping or a change in left-to-right behaviour. Especially scrutinise the corner-radius conversions in src/app/components/document-detail/document-detail.component.scss (`.btn-group .btn.order-0` / `.order-3`), document-card-large/small and pdf-editor (`.document-check`), and `.border-end`/`.border-start` in src/_app.scss which override Bootstrap classes that the RTL build also defines.
C. Confirm the RTL build and the LTR build can never both be active for one page, in both the Django-served path and the `ng serve` path, and that the inline script cannot double-apply the RTL sheet.
D. Check `is_bidi_language` and the template logic for edge cases: unknown locale codes, a user whose ui_settings language differs from the Django cookie language, unauthenticated users.
E. Look for directional CSS, inline styles, or JS-driven positioning ANYWHERE in src-ui/src or the Django templates under src/ that was MISSED and would stay wrong in RTL. Include grep terms like margin-left/right, padding-left/right, border-left/right, text-align, float, left:, right:, translateX, scrollLeft, object-position, background-position.
F. Flag anything that would break the left-to-right path or the production Docker build (`ng build --configuration production` builds all 37 locales; the Dockerfile then runs collectstatic).

Return: a short list of findings, each with file:line, severity, your confidence, and why it matters. Then a merge-risk verdict. Be concrete and skeptical; do not restate the change back to me. If you find nothing wrong in an area, say so in one line.

def is_bidi_language(language: str) -> bool:
    """
    Whether a language code such as "ar-AR" is written right-to-left.

    Django's language_info carries the bidi flag for every locale it knows
    about. Codes it does not know fall back to the language subtag, and are
    treated as left-to-right otherwise.
    """
    code = language.lower()
    try:
        return get_language_info(code)["bidi"]
    except KeyError:
        return code.split("-")[0] in settings.LANGUAGES_BIDI

I have enough evidence to report. Findings below; every file:line was read or grepped in this session.

### SUMMARY

The change is structurally sound and, as far as static analysis can prove, **LTR-neutral**: every logical-property mapping I checked is equivalent in LTR, the Django template links exactly one stylesheet, and `is_bidi_language` cannot raise on any input I could construct. No BLOCKER-grade defect survived.

What I **could not** confirm, and you should treat as open:
- **A (compilation):** not run — this role cannot execute builds (`sass`/`ng`/`pytest` are outside my read-only shell). I substituted a static equivalence argument (see EVIDENCE A) which is strong but not a byte-diff.
- **F (production artifact):** I could not run `ng build --configuration production`, so "`styles-rtl.css` exists in all 37 locale dirs" is reasoned, not observed (RISKS item 1). Everything else about the production/collectstatic path checked out.
- **The `ng serve` claim is false as implemented** (finding 1): nothing ever sets `dir` on the dev/standalone `index.html`, so that script is unreachable. Production (Django) RTL works through the template instead, so this is a gap in the dev/standalone path plus a wrong comment, not a regression.

Confirmed clean: B (all conversions), C for the Django path, D (unknown codes / mismatch / anonymous), E (no remaining directional literals except the corner-radius family in finding 3), F except the un-run build.

### EVIDENCE

**1. `src-ui/src/index.html:20-39` — MINOR, confidence high.** The RTL swap is dead code. `grep -rn`-equivalent probes: `git grep -n "documentElement" src-ui/src` returns only this script, `git grep -n "dir=" src-ui/src/**/*.html` returns **no** matches, and the file itself declares `<html lang="en" data-bs-theme="auto">` with no `dir`. `ng serve` (angular.json `serve.buildTarget`) serves this file verbatim; the per-locale built index.html inherits the same missing attribute (see the on-disk pre-change artifact `src/documents/static/frontend/ar-AR/index.html`). So the condition is never true, and the comment "it has to swap in the right-to-left bundle itself" is inaccurate. Why it matters: dev/standalone RTL never renders, and the only guard against double-loading in that path is unreachable. Fix: set direction from the compiled locale (e.g. in `main.ts`, before the swap: derive RTL from `LOCALE_ID`) or delete the script and fix the comment; also add `if (!document.querySelector('link[href="styles-rtl.css"]'))` so it cannot append a second RTL sheet if one is already present.

**2. `src/documents/templates/index.html:16` + `src-ui/angular.json:85-90` — MAJOR if wrong, confidence unverified (build not runnable here).** The template hard-links `frontend/<lang>/styles-rtl.css`. The installed `@angular-devkit/build-angular` browser schema (which `@angular-builders/custom-webpack:browser` extends) does support `{input, bundleName, inject}` (verified: `schema.json` styles-item properties at lines 55/91ff), and localized builds emit styles into each locale dir — `src/documents/static/frontend/ar-AR/styles.css` exists on disk — so the second bundle *should* land per locale. If it does not (emitted once at the build root, or dropped for non-default locales), Arabic/Persian users get a 404 stylesheet and a completely unstyled app while LTR locales are unaffected. Must be checked by running the production build and `ls src/documents/static/frontend/*/styles-rtl.css` (37 dirs), and by grepping one copy for `.ms-1{margin-right` (RTL mirror present).

**3. Missed physical corner radii — MINOR each, confidence high (grep-verified), aggregate is the weakest part of the feature.** These are exactly the pattern the change converted elsewhere, and they are all inline-flow-relative controls, so in RTL the wrong corners get squared:
- `src-ui/src/_app.scss:353-354` (`.paperless-input-select .input-group ng-select:not(:last-child) .ng-select-container`)
- `src-ui/src/_app.scss:706-712` (`.btn-group-xs` first/last-child radii)
- `src-ui/src/_app.scss:803-810` (`pngx-preview-popup:not(:last-child)/:not(:first-child) > .btn` — note the `margin-inline-start` two lines above *was* converted, so this looks like an oversight)
- `src-ui/src/app/components/admin/tasks/tasks.component.scss:63-66` and `src-ui/src/app/components/document-list/filter-editor/filter-editor.component.scss:12-15` (`.input-group .dropdown .btn`)
- `src-ui/src/app/components/common/confirm-button/confirm-button.component.scss:1-12` (physical copy of Bootstrap's input/btn-group rules — the RTL build mirrors Bootstrap's own, but not this custom selector)
- `src-ui/src/app/components/common/custom-fields-query-dropdown/custom-fields-query-dropdown.component.scss:8-11,15-18,29-30` (`.ng-select-container`, `.rounded-end`, `.doc-link-select`, all `!important`)
Fix: same logical mapping used elsewhere (`border-top-right-radius:0; border-bottom-right-radius:0` → `border-start-end-radius:0; border-end-end-radius:0`, and vice versa).

**4. `src-ui/src/app/components/app-frame/global-search/global-search.component.scss:42` — NIT, confidence medium.** `transition: all .3s ease, padding-inline-start 0s ease` — the 0s entry exists to suppress the `all` entry for that one property ("Safari requires all"). If a browser does not match logical properties in `transition-property`, the padding animation returns (visible focus jitter). Cheap hardening: list the physical name too.

**5. `src/documents/static/bootstrap.rtl.min.css` is untracked — NIT, confidence high.** If the commit misses it, `base.html:17` 404s and RTL auth pages get no Bootstrap at all. Verified otherwise good: byte-size identical to `src-ui/node_modules/bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.rtl.min.css` (232219 = 232219) and to the committed `bootstrap.min.css` counterpart (232111 = 232111), both v5.3.8 matching `package.json` `bootstrap: ^5.3.8`; contains no `[dir=rtl]` selectors (compiled RTL variant, `grep -c "dir=rtl"` → 0); not excluded by `.dockerignore` and collectable from the app static dir (no `STATICFILES_DIRS` override; `grep bootstrap Dockerfile` → no matches).

**6. Direction source differs between auth pages and the SPA — MINOR, confidence high.** `base.html:4-6` uses Django's cookie-derived language, `views.py:338-353,364-365` prefers `ui_settings.settings["language"]`. A logged-in user whose stored UI language differs from the cookie (e.g. cookie `en-us`, ui language `ar-ar`) sees an LTR auth/2FA page and then an RTL SPA. Within the SPA itself bundle and direction come from the *same* `frontend_language`, so they cannot disagree.

**Confirmed good (no findings):**
- **B:** every conversion verified as LTR-equivalent and correctly flipped in RTL, including the ones you flagged: `.order-0`/`.order-3` (top-right≡start-end etc.), `.dropdown-toggle-split`, `.document-check` in pdf-editor/card-large/card-small (`top-left+bottom-right` → `start-start+end-end`), `text-align: start`, `float: inline-end`, `.dropdown-menu-right` (`inset-inline-end/start`). `_app.scss:321-325` `.border-end`/`.border-start` overrides match the RTL build's mirrored definitions (verified in `node_modules/.../bootstrap.rtl.css:7494` → `.border-end{border-left:…}`), and `theme.scss:210` `border-inline-end: none` removes the same physical edge the RTL build's `.border-end` adds. `document-detail.component.scss:36` `padding-inline-end: 2.5em` matches the RTL build's left-side arrow (`bootstrap.rtl.css:2320` `background-position: left .75rem center`); the `select.component.scss` RTL override has strictly higher specificity than the LTR rule and mirrors to the side the RTL build itself uses (`bootstrap.rtl.css:2914`) — and has no logical form, so the `:host-context` exception is justified.
- **C (Django path):** `git grep "styles_css" src` and `"styles.css" src src-ui/src` show exactly one link site (`templates/index.html:16`); the Angular-built `frontend/<locale>/index.html` is *not* served (Django uses `IndexView.template_name = "index.html"` → `src/documents/templates/index.html`, urls.py:414), so the inline script cannot interact with the Django link.
- **D:** `is_bidi_language` is safe on every input — read the installed Django (`.venv/.../django/utils/translation/__init__.py:269-288`): `get_language_info` raises **only** `KeyError`, including for dash-less unknown codes, and it looks up `LANG_INFO` *without* lowercasing, so the explicit `.lower()` in `views.py:327` is load-bearing (the uppercase `ar-AR` from `get_frontend_language` would otherwise miss and fall through). The `LANGUAGES_BIDI` fallback is real: it is not overridden by paperless (`grep LANGUAGES_BIDI src/paperless/settings/__init__.py` → none) and Django's default is `["he","ar","ar-dz","ckb","fa","ug","ur"]` (`global_settings.py:156`), covering the fallback paths in the new tests; `LANGUAGES` has lowercase codes `("ar-ar")`, `("fa-ir")` (`settings/__init__.py:530-531,546`), so `get_frontend_language` → `ar-AR`/`fa-IR` as the tests assert. Anonymous users never reach `IndexView` (`login_required`, `src/paperless/urls.py:414`) and `AnonymousUser.username` is `""` anyway; auth pages for anonymous users resolve direction via `{% get_current_language_bidi %}` with `{% load i18n %}` present.
- **E:** after the change, `git grep` over `src-ui/src/**/*.scss|*.html|*.ts` finds **no** `padding-left/right`, `border-left/right`, `float: left/right`, `text-align: left/right`, `translateX`, `scrollLeft`, `offsetLeft`, and no directional inline styles; remaining `margin-left/right` are only `print.scss:11-12` (both set to 0 on the same element — direction-neutral) and a comment. Remaining `left:`/`right:` are symmetric or full-width: `document-detail.component.scss:25-26` (30%/30%), `upload-file-widget.component.scss:35-37` (0/0), `toasts.component.scss:4` and `clearable-badge.component.scss:26` (centred), `pdf-viewer.component.scss:56` (100%-width canvas). `src/documents/static/base.css` `.form-stacked-*` radii zero both sides. `src-ui/src/app/components/common/pdf-viewer/pdf-viewer.component.scss:128-135` (`.begin`/`.end` highlight radii) stays physical but tracks the *document* text direction (PDF.js), not UI direction — defensible, NIT only.
- **F (aside from the un-run build):** the angular.json style-object shape is schema-valid for the installed builder; no other file references `styles.scss`/`styles-rtl` except angular.json, the new template/views/tests, and a now-slightly-stale comment at `select.component.scss:1`; no test asserts the old `lang="en"`; collectstatic needs no Dockerfile change; budgets have headroom (on-disk production artifacts: main.js 2.90 MB + styles.css 357 KB + polyfills 36 KB ≈ 3.3 MB, +~0.36 MB for the second sheet vs the 5 MB `initial` error threshold).

**A (static equivalence, not a compile):** `_app.scss` is 820 lines vs the old 816 — exactly consistent with +7 comment lines, −1 blank-line-absorbed effect, and the two removed `@import`s (fonts, bootstrap) now living in `_fonts.scss`/`_bootstrap-ltr.scss`, which are `@use`d *before* `_app` (`styles.scss:10-12`). The relative order of the three plain-CSS imports and of `meta.load-css("theme")` / ng-select / `meta.load-css("print")` / body is unchanged (`_app.scss:3-16`), and `_app.scss` lines 1-820 contain no other directional change than the logical-property substitutions I reviewed; whatever hoisting the downstream CSS pipeline applies (the pre-change `frontend/en-US/styles.css` already shows fonts-import-first and ng-select before bootstrap) it receives the same statement sequence in the same order.

### CHANGES

None. (Read-only review; no file was created, modified, or staged. Only inspection commands were run.)

### RISKS

1. `frontend/<locale>/styles-rtl.css` emission per locale is unverified (finding 2) — the single highest-value pre-merge check.
2. RTL coverage is incomplete in the corner-radius family (finding 3); RTL users will see small corner artifacts on input/button groups and in the PDF preview popup, and the change has no RTL visual test (no screenshot/e2e evidence exists in the diff; the only new tests are Django-side).
3. Dev/standalone RTL is not actually implemented (finding 1), so anyone validating this change with `ng serve --configuration ar-AR` will see LTR and may wrongly conclude the feature is broken.
4. Auth pages keep their own direction source (finding 6), so the two halves of the app can disagree for users with `ui_settings.language` set.
5. `src-ui/src/index.html` still hardcodes `lang="en"` (unrelated to findings, but it is now inconsistent with the Django template's `lang="{{ frontend_language }}"`).

### BLOCKERS

None — no BLOCKER-severity defect found. Blocked probes (capability, not permission refusals): `node_modules/.bin/sass` compilation of old-vs-new stylesheets, `ng build --configuration production`, and running `pytest src/documents/tests/test_views.py`/`src/paperless/tests/test_api_auth.py` were all unavailable to this read-only reviewer role; findings 1/2 and my A conclusion are correspondingly static-only.
